correctness.rationale: The support-function identity yields exactly the three trigonometric arcs. Counting inverse images and differentiating gives the complete density with Haar normalization 2/pi. The interior maximum exists iff q>1 and pq<1; in the ordered subregion p+q<sqrt(1+q²)<2 the only divergence heights are r(p+q), r sqrt(1+q²), and 2r. One, two, one inverse branches respectively yield the exact coefficients 2/pi,4/pi,2/pi. Since r>0, q>1, algebraic inversion is unambiguous, and cusp derivatives are nonzero. Standalone checker validated normalization across regimes, ordered critical coefficients and scale/parameter reconstruction. No finite checks replace proof.

value.rationale: The 2022 paper identifies the asymmetric kite as an apparently optimal four-gon candidate yet studies only the first two angular width moments. The complete three-regime angular critical-point law produces a natural geometric phase classification. In the physically motivated ordered subregion containing the candidate, a measurable unlabeled one-dimensional width law has exactly three sharp singularities that recover all scale and shape data with an explicit smooth inverse. This is a motivated geometric tomography fact rather than a relabeling or arbitrary numerical slice.
